prompts.prompt: Read the Python 3.13 changelog at https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.13.html and summarize the top 5 new features. The page is long, so make sure you get content beyond the first section.
assertions: Uses fetch tool with the docs.python.org URL
Uses start_index or max_length parameters to read beyond the first chunk
Returns content as markdown (not raw HTML) for clean summarization
Baseline must fall back to curl/Invoke-WebRequest and parse raw HTML manually

with_skill.plan: 1. Call fetch(url='https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.13.html', max_length=5000) to get the first chunk. 2. Call fetch(url='...', start_index=5000, max_length=5000) to get subsequent chunks. 3. Continue fetching chunks until enough feature content is gathered. 4. Summarize the top 5 features from the clean markdown output.

baseline.plan: 1. Use curl or Invoke-WebRequest to download the raw HTML page. 2. Attempt to parse the HTML manually or pipe through a text converter if available. 3. Struggle with raw HTML tags, navigation chrome, and page length. 4. Try to extract feature descriptions from noisy output. May partially succeed but with significant effort and messy results.

prompts.prompt: Fetch the raw HTML source of https://example.com and count how many anchor tags it contains.
assertions: Should call fetch with the raw=true parameter to get unprocessed HTML
Should correctly use the raw mode rather than default markdown conversion
Should parse the returned HTML to count <a> tags and report the number
Baseline can use curl to get raw HTML but lacks the integrated fetch tool's raw parameter

with_skill.plan: 1. Call fetch(url='https://example.com', raw=True) to get the raw HTML source. 2. Parse the HTML output and count occurrences of <a> or anchor tags. 3. Report the count to the user.

baseline.plan: 1. Run curl https://example.com to download raw HTML. 2. Pipe through grep -c '<a ' to count anchor tags. This actually works reasonably well for this simple case since curl returns raw HTML by default.

prompts.prompt: Compare the homepages of https://httpbin.org and https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com by fetching both and telling me which has more content and what each site offers.
assertions: Should call fetch twice, once for each URL
Should use max_length to control response size for each fetch
Should compare the two pages based on content length and topic coverage
Baseline can curl both URLs but gets raw HTML that is harder to compare meaningfully

with_skill.plan: 1. Call fetch(url='https://httpbin.org', max_length=5000) and fetch(url='https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com', max_length=5000) in parallel. 2. Compare the markdown content length and structure of each. 3. Summarize what each site offers and which has more content.

baseline.plan: 1. Run curl for both URLs to get raw HTML. 2. Attempt to read through HTML tags and navigation elements to understand page content. 3. Compare raw byte sizes. The HTML noise makes meaningful content comparison difficult without manual cleanup.
